gloss: be one, be joined; together, as one, alike; only, alone
summary: To be one: people or things joined so that they are, go, act or suffer as one, and the one who stands alone. The adverbs יַחַד and יַחְדָּו (about 140 times) say “together”: two walking in company (Amo 3:3), a people answering with one voice (Exo 19:8), kings taking counsel against Yahweh and his anointed (Psa 2:2), and “all alike”, the whole without exception (Psa 14:3, quoted at Rom 3:12; Job 34:15). The verb is to join oneself (Gen 49:6) and, in the piel, to make one: “unite my heart to fear your name” (Psa 86:11). יָחִיד is the only one, above all the only son: Isaac, “your son, your only one, whom you love” (Gen 22:2), the pattern the New Testament takes up for God's only begotten Son (Heb 11:17; Jhn 3:16). Arabic waḥada “be one, alone”, Geʿez ተወሐደ “be united” and ዋሕድ “only, only begotten”, and Jewish Aramaic יַחֵד “unite” show the same root.

words.summary: About 95 times, also spelled יַחְדָּיו (Jer 46:12, 21; 49:3), the commonest word of the root. It is יַחַד with an adverbial ending. It says that two or more are in one place, act as one, or share one lot.

senses.definition: In one place or on one road at the same time: two who live, walk, eat or lie down side by side.

evidence.note: “Do two walk יַחְדָּו unless they have agreed to meet?” Being together implies an agreement.
“The land could not bear them to dwell יַחְדָּו, for their possessions were great”: Abram and Lot in one place, and then parted (Gen 13:9, 11).
Abraham and Isaac, carrying the wood, the fire and the knife: “and the two of them went יַחְדָּו”; again at Gen 22:8.
Abraham and his young men “went יַחְדָּו to Beersheba”.
Esau and Jacob: “too great for them to dwell together”, as Gen 13:6.
“If brothers dwell יַחְדָּו and one of them dies”: brothers on one inheritance.
“We were together; there was no stranger with us in the house.”
Ishmael and his men “ate bread there together in Mizpah”.
“In peace I will both (יַחְדָּו) lie down and sleep, for you alone, Yahweh, make me dwell in safety.”
“We who together made counsel sweet; we walked in the house of God.”
“The calf and the young lion and the fatling יַחְדָּו, and a little child shall lead them”: beasts that now prey on one another lying down together in the kingdom.
“The cow and the bear shall feed; their young shall lie down יַחְדָּו.”

senses.gloss: together, as one, with one voice or purpose
senses.definition: Many acting as one body: answering, singing, gathering, taking counsel or going up as one.

evidence.note: “All the people answered יַחְדָּו and said, All that Yahweh has spoken we will do.”
“Magnify Yahweh with me, and let us exalt his name יַחְדָּו.”
“The voice of your watchmen! They lift up the voice, יַחְדָּו they sing for joy, for eye to eye they see the return of Yahweh to Zion.”
“Break forth, sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem, for Yahweh has comforted his people.”
The kings “gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one mouth (פֶּה אֶחָד)”.
“They all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem.”
“Come, let us meet together (וְנִוָּעֲדָה יַחְדָּו)”, said Sanballat and Geshem, meaning harm.
“Those who watch for my life take counsel together.”
“They take counsel with one heart (לֵב יַחְדָּו) against you; they make a covenant.”
“Let them take counsel together: who told this of old? Is it not I, Yahweh? And there is no other God besides me.”
“Let all the nations be gathered together.”
“When the peoples are gathered together, and the kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.”
“In those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I gave as an inheritance to your fathers.”
“The sons of Judah and the sons of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head (רֹאשׁ אֶחָד), and go up from the land.”
“The sons of Israel shall come, they and the sons of Judah together, weeping as they go, and they shall seek Yahweh their God.”
The blind and the lame, the woman with child and her that travails, together: “a great company shall return here.”
“Young men and old together” rejoice in the dance.

senses.definition: The whole of a group without exception, sharing one lot or one character, often with כֹּל or כֻּלָּם.

evidence.note: “All have turned aside, יַחְדָּו they have become corrupt; there is none who does good, not even one (אֶחָד).” Paul quotes it: “they have all together (ἅμα) become worthless” (Rom 3:12).
The same words: “every one has gone back; together they have become corrupt.”
“All turned aside, together (ἅμα) they became worthless”, from Psa 14:3 (Peshitta כֻּלְּהוֹן סְטַו אַכְחְדָא, “all turned aside together”), to show that all, Jew and Greek, are under sin (Rom 3:9).
“Are not my commanders all alike kings?”
“Fathers and sons together shall stumble on them.”
“The destruction of transgressors and sinners together.”
“Transgressors shall be destroyed together.”
“The helper shall stumble and the helped shall fall, and they shall all of them (יַחְדָּו כֻּלָּם) come to an end together.”
“They are ashamed … all of them together.”
“The glory of Yahweh shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together.”
“The unclean and the clean alike may eat it.”
“Your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together.”
“The judgments of Yahweh are true; they are righteous altogether.”
Chariot and horse, army and warrior: “together they lie down, they shall not rise.”

senses.definition: Of two things fastened or set side by side as one: boards coupled, a mixed yoke, a mixed cloth, a city built compactly.

evidence.note: The corner boards “shall be doubled below, and together (וְיַחְדָּו) they shall be complete at its top, to the one ring”.
“You shall not plough with an ox and a donkey together.”
“You shall not wear mixed cloth, wool and linen together.”
“Jerusalem, built as a city that is joined (שֶׁחֻבְּרָה) together.”
“ἅμα ἠχρειώθησαν”, quoting Psa 14:3.
“We who are alive … shall be caught up together (ἅμα) with them”: the living and the raised dead gathered as one at the Lord's coming.

greek.gloss: with one mind, with one accord

evidence.locator: Job.34.15, יַחַד → ὁμοθυμαδόν; ὁμοθυμαδόν renders the two adverbs (one shared token list) about 15 times

evidence.note: “That with one accord (ὁμοθυμαδόν), with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ”: the “let us exalt his name together” of Psa 34:4.
The disciples “lifted up their voice to God with one accord”, and then quoted Psa 2:1–2.

parallels.note: Gathered together under one head, conspiring with one mouth; “together corrupt … not even one”.

opposites.note: Abram and Lot could not dwell together, and so parted (וַיִּפָּרְדוּ).

phrases.gloss: and the two of them went together

words.gloss: unitedness, union; (as adverb) together, all alike
words.summary: About 45 times, pausal יָחַד. Once a noun, “union” (1Ch 12:18); otherwise an adverb in the same senses as יַחְדָּו, mostly in poetry (Job, Psalms, Isaiah).

senses.definition: Being one with another: hearts joined in one purpose.

evidence.note: David to the men of Benjamin and Judah: “If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart shall be toward you לְיָחַד, for union”; set against “to betray me to my adversaries”.
“There was a king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, יַחַד the tribes of Israel”: the tribes as one people.

senses.definition: As יַחְדָּו: in one place, or acting as one.

evidence.note: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell גַּם־יָחַד, even as one.”

“The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together (נוֹסְדוּ־יָחַד) against Yahweh and against his anointed.” Quoted at Act 4:26, where Herod and Pilate, the nations and the peoples of Israel, “were gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed” (Act 4:27).
“The rulers were gathered together (συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό) against the Lord and against his Christ”, from Psa 2:2.
“I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will set them together (יַחַד) as sheep in a fold.”
“You have nothing to do with us in building a house to our God, but we ourselves together will build to Yahweh.”
“While they take counsel together against me.”
“All who hate me whisper together against me.”
“When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.”
“Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains sing for joy together.”
“Who will contend with me? Let us stand up together.”
“Let us plead together.”
The Ammonites “were scattered, so that no two of them were left together”.
“His troops come together and encamp around my tent.”

senses.definition: As יַחְדָּו: every one of a group sharing one lot, above all the one end of death that wise and foolish, rich and poor, share.

evidence.note: “All flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust.”
“He sees that wise men die; the fool and the brutish perish alike, and leave their wealth to others.”
“Both low and high, rich and poor together”: all men addressed alike.
The prosperous man and the bitter in soul: “they lie down alike in the dust, and the worm covers them.”
In death, “the prisoners are at ease together; they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.”
“Will it go down to the bars of the grave (שְׁאֹל)? Shall we rest together in the dust?”
“Hide them in the dust together.”
“Men of low degree are vapour, men of rank a lie; in the balances they go up; they are together lighter than vapour.”
Yahweh “fashions their hearts alike, he considers all their works”.
“Let the wicked fall into their own nets together.”

evidence.locator: Psa.2.2, נוֹסְדוּ־יָחַד → συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό (MACULA aligns the verb only)

evidence.note: The Septuagint of Psa 2:2 quoted word for word.

words.gloss: only, only one; alone, solitary; (my) only one, my life
words.summary: Twelve times. The one who has no other beside him: an only child, the one alone and without help, and in two psalms “my only one”, one's own life. The only son is the measure of grief (Jer 6:26; Amo 8:10; Zec 12:10) and of what Abraham did not withhold (Gen 22:12, 16).

senses.definition: A son or daughter with no brother or sister: the one child of a parent, and so the most dear, whose loss is the bitterest mourning.

evidence.note: “Take your son, your only one (יְחִידְךָ), whom you love, Isaac”: though Ishmael lived, Isaac was the only son of the promise (Gen 21:12).
“You have not withheld your son, your only one, from me.”
“Because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son, your only one, I will surely bless you … and in your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.”
Jephthah's daughter: “she was his only one (יְחִידָה); besides her he had neither son nor daughter”.
“I was a son to my father, tender and only one (וְיָחִיד) in the sight of my mother.”
“Make mourning as for an only son (אֵבֶל יָחִיד), most bitter lamentation.”
“I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.”

“They shall look on me whom they pierced, and they shall mourn for him as one mourns for the only son (הַיָּחִיד), and weep bitterly over him as one weeps over a firstborn.” Quoted at Jhn 19:37 and Rev 1:7.
“They shall look on him whom they pierced”, from Zec 12:10, fulfilled at the cross.
“By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac … his only begotten (τὸν μονογενῆ)”: the Greek for the יָחִיד of Gen 22.

senses.definition: One left by himself, with no companion or kin to help him.

evidence.note: “Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I am alone (יָחִיד) and afflicted.”
“God makes the solitary (יְחִידִים) dwell in a house; he brings out prisoners into prosperity”, beside “a father of the fatherless and judge of the widows” (Psa 68:6).

senses.definition: In parallel with נַפְשִׁי: one's own single life, which once lost cannot be replaced.

evidence.note: “Deliver my soul (נַפְשִׁי) from the sword, my only one (יְחִידָתִי) from the power of the dog.”
“Rescue my soul from their ravages, my only one from the lions.”

evidence.locator: Jdg.11.34 → μονογενής; Psa.22.21; 35.17 → μονογενῆ; Psa.25.16 → μονογενής

evidence.note: Isaac, “his only begotten”, of Gen 22.
“God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten (μονογενῆ) Son”: the gift of Gen 22:16, “you have not withheld your son, your only one”.
“God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.”
The dead man at Nain, “the only begotten son of his mother, and she was a widow”.

evidence.locator: Jer.6.26; Amo.8.10 → ἀγαπητοῦ; Zec.12.10 → ἀγαπητόν; at Gen.22.2, 12, 16 the Septuagint's τὸν υἱόν σου τὸν ἀγαπητόν stands for בִּנְךָ אֶת־יְחִידְךָ (MACULA aligns יָחִיד with the article)

evidence.note: “You are my beloved Son (ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός), in you I am well pleased”: the Septuagint's word for Isaac, the יָחִיד of Gen 22:2.
“Having yet one son, his beloved (ἕνα υἱὸν … ἀγαπητόν), he sent him last to them.”

words.gloss: be joined, join oneself; (piel) unite, make one
words.summary: Three times: twice in the qal, joining oneself to a company (always negated), and once in the piel, making the heart one. Pro 27:17 יָחַד is the verb חָדַד “sharpen”, filed here by spelling.

senses.gloss: be joined with, join oneself to
senses.definition: To become one with a company and share its counsel or its lot.

evidence.note: Jacob of Simeon and Levi: “Let my soul not come into their council; let my glory not be joined (אַל־תֵּחַד) to their assembly (בִּקְהָלָם)”, parallel to “come into their council”.
Of the king of Babylon: “You shall not be joined with them (לֹא־תֵחַד אִתָּם) in burial”, not laid with the kings who lie in honour (Isa 14:18–19).

senses.definition: To make the heart one, undivided in its fear of Yahweh.

evidence.note: “Teach me your way, Yahweh; I will walk in your truth; unite (יַחֵד) my heart to fear your name”: the opposite of the divided heart (לֵב וָלֵב, Psa 12:3; Jas 1:8).
The double heart, “with a heart and a heart they speak”.
“I will give them one heart (לֵב אֶחָד) and one way, that they may fear me for ever”: the gift the psalmist prays for, in other words.

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for μονογενής (SEDRA lexeme 1369, ܝܚܝܕܝܐ): the only child of a parent, and above all the only begotten Son of God.

senses.definition: The one child of a father or mother; of Jesus, the one Son God begot and gave.

evidence.note: Peshitta: God “gave his Son, the only begotten (יִחִידָיָא)”.
Peshitta: “in the name of the only begotten Son (דִּיחִידָיָא) of God”.
Peshitta: “glory as of the only begotten (דִּיחִידָיָא) who is from the Father”.
Peshitta: “the only begotten (יִחִידָיָא) God, who is in the bosom of his Father, he has declared him.”
Peshitta: “God sent his only begotten Son (יִחִידָיָא) into the world.”
Peshitta: a dead man carried out, “who was the only one (דִּיחִידָיָא) of his mother, and she was a widow”.
Peshitta: Jairus “had an only daughter (יִחִידָיתָּא)”.
Peshitta: “Look upon my son, for he is my only one (בְּרִי דִּיחִידָיָא הוּ לִי).”

words.summary: SEDRA lexeme 3533, ܝܚܝܕܐ, the form of the Peshitta's one verse with it, Heb 11:17, where it renders μονογενής of Isaac, as Jewish Aramaic יְחִידָא does in the Targum of Gen 22:2.

senses.definition: Isaac, Abraham's only son, offered up.

evidence.note: Peshitta: Abraham offered Isaac, “and offered up his only one (וְלִיחִידֵהּ)”, he who had received the promises.

words.summary: SEDRA lexeme 1370, ܡܫܘܚܕܐ, a participle of the Syriac verb's causative stem (“left alone”). Once in the Peshitta's New Testament.

senses.definition: A widow left by herself, with no family to support her.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “she who is a widow indeed and desolate (וַמְשַׁוְחַדְתָּא)” (μεμονωμένη, “left alone”) sets her hope on God.

cognates.gloss: be one, be alone; (II) make one; (VIII) become one; one; alone, solitary
cognates.note: The Hebrew's y- is the w- of Arabic (as yāḏaʿ / wadaʿa). Lane's article carries both sides of the Hebrew root: being one and alone (waḥīd “a man alone, by himself, solitary”, as יָחִיד) and being made one (form II “he made it one”, form VIII “it became one”, as the piel “unite my heart” and the adverbs). Arabic shows ḥ, not ḫ, behind ח.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2926, art. وحد, وَحَدَ (n41729)
evidence.note: “He was, or became, alone, by himself.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2927, art. وحد, وحّدهُ (n41730) and form 8 اِتَّحَدَ
evidence.note: Form 2: “He made it one; or called it one … He asserted, or declared, God to be one.” Form 8: “It was, or became, one … It (a number of things, two and more) became one.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2928, art. وحد, وَحِيدٌ (n41741) and وَاحِدٌ (n41742)
evidence.note: وَحِيدٌ “A man alone; by himself; apart from others; solitary; lonely”; وَاحِدٌ “One; the first of the numbers … one alone: a single person or thing.”

cognates.gloss: be united, be one; only, only begotten
cognates.note: Geʿez has both halves of the Hebrew: the verb “be made one, be united” (of man and wife made one), and ዋሕድ “only, only begotten”, the Geʿez New Testament's word at Luk 8:42, Jhn 1:14; 3:16 and 1Jn 4:9 where the Peshitta has יְחִידָיָא. Geʿez writes ḥ (ሐ), not ḫ (ኀ).

evidence.note: ተወሐደ “uniri, unum esse vel fieri: matrimonio”; ተዋሐደ “inter sese uniri, adunari, in unum conjungi”; ዋሕድ “unicus, unigenitus … Luc. 8, 42; in specie de Filio Dei unigenito Joh. 1, 14. 3, 16; 1 Joh. 4, 9”. Read from the OCR text of the vendored copy; the page link is reckoned from other entries' column-to-page offsets and should be checked.

evidence.locator: SEM001076 wḥd [unite], GEZ006070 wḥd [unite]; ARM011736 YḤD [unite]; HEB002923 yaḥad [join]

cognates.gloss: (pael) unite, concentrate (the heart); (ithpaal) be joined; only, only one
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums, the same root and senses: the Targum of Psa 86:11 keeps the pael for “unite my heart”, the ithpaal “be joined” stands in the Targum of Gen 49:6, and יְחִידָא is the only son in the Targums of Gen 22:2, Jdg 11:34 and Pro 4:3.

evidence.locator: s.v. יְחַד (ch.), citing Targ. Ps. LXXXVI, 11 (Pa. יַחֵד, concentrate); Targ. Y. Ex. XIX, 2 (part. pass. מְיַחַד, united, harmonious); Targ. Y. I Gen. XLIX, 6 (Ithpa., be joined)
s.v. יָחִיד (ch.), יְחִידָא, citing Targ. Gen. XXII, 2; Targ. Prov. IV, 3; Targ. Jud. XI, 34 (fem. יְחִידָאָה)

cognates.note: Akkadian, which lost ḥ, has w- at the start as Arabic and Geʿez do, and the sense of יָחִיד: alone, the only one, a lone person.

evidence.note: Senses “alone”, “only”, “single”, “solitary”.
“alone; free-standing; lone (person); only; single; sole”.

cognates.note: With y- as Hebrew and ḥ (Ugaritic keeps ḥ and ḫ apart). Known here only from Wiktionary; not yet checked in DULAT or a text edition, so recorded as possible.

Ugaritic “one” (aḥd) with the adverbial -h, “together”, which Segert sets beside Hebrew יַחְדָּו. It is the ʾḥd form of “one” (Hebrew אֶחָד), not the yḥd/wḥd form, so it shows the adverb's sense rather than this root's own spelling: possible only.

evidence.note: “aḥdh with adverbial -h ‘at once, together’ (cf. H. yaḥdāw)”. Read from the OCR text.

doctrine.statement: Abraham's יָחִיד was Isaac, the son born to him by promise in his old age (Gen 21:1–3, 12), whom he was told to offer and did not withhold (Gen 22:2, 12, 16); on that act God swore that in his seed all nations would be blessed (Gen 22:16–18). The New Testament uses the same word for Isaac, “his only begotten” (Heb 11:17), and for Jesus: God “gave his only begotten Son” (Jhn 3:16; 1Jn 4:9), and “spared not his own Son” (Rom 8:32), the words of Gen 22:16. The voice at the Jordan, “my beloved Son” (Mrk 1:11), is the Septuagint's word for Isaac the יָחִיד. As Isaac was begotten by Abraham and born in time, Jesus is the only begotten Son because God begot him: the holy spirit, the power of the Highest, came upon Mary, “therefore the holy one born shall be called the Son of God” (Luk 1:35). An only begotten son is a son who has a father before him, not one without beginning.

יַחַד puts all men in one lot at death: “all flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust” (Job 34:15); “wise men die; the fool and the brutish perish alike” (Psa 49:11); the prosperous and the bitter “lie down alike in the dust, and the worm covers them” (Job 21:26); in death the prisoners “are at ease together; they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster” (Job 3:18), and Job asks whether he will “rest together in the dust” in the grave (Job 17:16). The verses speak of dust, worm, rest and silence, not of a soul living on elsewhere: man returns to the dust he was taken from (Gen 3:19), and the wise man has no advantage there over the fool (Psa 49:11–13). Hope lies in the resurrection, when the living and the raised dead are “caught up together” with them to meet the Lord (1Th 4:16–17).

The prophets use יַחְדָּו for Judah and Israel gathered as one people again: they “shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I gave as an inheritance to your fathers” (Jer 3:18); “gathered together, they shall appoint for themselves one head, and go up from the land” (Hos 2:2); they come “together, weeping, and seek Yahweh their God” (Jer 50:4); the remnant is set “together as sheep in a fold” (Mic 2:12). The land is the land promised to the fathers, and the one head is the king of David's line (Hos 3:5). The same day brings the creation at peace, wolf and lamb and calf and lion “together” (Isa 11:6–7), and “all flesh shall see” the glory of Yahweh “together” (Isa 40:5). These are the kingdom of God on earth, not a heaven going.

Zechariah foretells that the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem “shall look on me whom they pierced, and mourn for him as one mourns for the only son (הַיָּחִיד)” (Zec 12:10). John cites it at the piercing of Jesus' side (Jhn 19:34, 37), and Revelation of his coming: “every eye shall see him, and those who pierced him, and all the tribes of the land shall mourn over him” (Rev 1:7). The one pierced is mourned as an only son because he is the only begotten Son; the mourning of Jerusalem's own people is still to come, when he returns.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. Root key יחד, as the corpus and BDB key it; no entry had it. אֶחָד “one” (a.cj.aa), Aramaic and Syriac חַד, and the noun phrases with כְּאֶחָד stay in echad.json (root אחד), which already names יחד as a separate root that cognates suggest may go back to the same older word (Arabic wāḥid beside ʾaḥad, Akkadian wēdu, Ugaritic aḥd beside yḥd); this entry does not move any of them. akk-wedu is cited here too because its sense is יָחִיד's. BDB keys: j.be.ac (יַחַד, BDB 45) and j.be.ad (יַחְדָּו, BDB 92) share ONE token list of 141 in the corpus (about 95 יַחְדָּו/יַחְדָּיו, 45 יַחַד/יָחַד, counted from the text), so the shared surface count does not distinguish them. The two distinct source lemmas retain their respective keys. j.be.ab יָחִיד, j.be.aa the verb. Pro 27:17 יָחַד/יַחַד is חָדַד “sharpen” (h.aq.aa), filed here by spelling. a.ci.aj אָחַד is a zero-token cross-reference (“see יחד, see חדד”), not claimed. Names: Jahdo (j.be.ae, 1Ch 5:14) in names/jahdo.json. Left out: Jahzerah (יַחְזֵרָה, j.be.aj, 1Ch 9:12), which BDB files under this root but whose letters (יחזר) do not contain it; it more likely belongs to חזר, and with its parallel Ahzai (אַחְזַי, Neh 11:13) to אחז; to be written there. Also not here: Jahdiel (יַחְדִּיאֵל, 1Ch 5:24) and Jehdeiah (יֶחְדְּיָהוּ), which BDB derives from חדה “rejoice”, and Jahath (יַחַת). Syriac: SEDRA root 819 ;KD; lexemes 1369 (only, only begotten; Greek link μονογενής ×8), 3533 (Heb 11:17 only), 1370 (1Ti 5:5 only) entered as syc words; 1368 the verb (separate; kindle) has no New Testament token and is not entered. The vocalisation of מְשַׁוְחְדָא (SEDRA MWaOKD'oA) is my reading and should be checked. Peshitta readings were taken from the SEDRA word tables in data/haqor.db, the verse notes' wording otherwise from the Greek; Luk 9:38 has דִּיחִידָיָא. Rom 3:12: the Peshitta has אַכְחְדָא “together” (SEDRA lexeme אכחדא, a different word). Psa 2:2: MACULA aligns only the verb with συνήχθησαν; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό for יָחַד is the Septuagint's text as quoted in Act 4:26. Gen 22:2 ἀγαπητός: MACULA aligns יְחִידְךָ with the article τόν; the claim that ἀγαπητόν stands for it rests on the Septuagint's wording. Dillmann read from the OCR text only (garbled); the column and archive.org page should be checked against the scan. Not consulted: DULAT for Ugaritic yḥd (only Wiktionary), Leslau for Geʿez, Biella/SabaWeb for Sabaic wḥd “one” (a lead from the other lexicons), Payne Smith for the Syriac verb ܐܘܚܕ/ܫܘܚܕ. Open questions: (1) whether יַחְדָּו and יַחַד should be one word (the corpus does not separate them; BDB does); (2) the son-of-god doctrine reads μονογενής as “only begotten”, a son with a beginning, from Isaac and Luk 1:35; (3) the-pierced-one reads Zec 12:10 and Rev 1:7 of a mourning in Jerusalem at Christ's return.
